neighbours.label: the token right after a phrase naming a person's innate trait or appetite (a sweet tooth, an appetite for adventure, a love of order)
fire: My uncle has a terrible temper, so the children avoid him at dinner.
She always had a thirst for knowledge that her teachers noticed.
Like many cats, he has a strong curiosity about every closed door.
Ever since childhood I have had a fear of heights, so I skip the balcony.
Her knack for languages was obvious by the age of six.
He has a stubborn streak that his parents found exhausting.
Tom has a weakness for chocolate, so he hides it from himself.
People with an introverted nature often need quiet time to recharge.
quiet: My uncle has a terrible cough, so the children avoid him at dinner.
She always had a stack of books that her teachers noticed.
Like many old houses, it has a strong door at every entrance.
Ever since the storm we have had a crack in the wall, so we skip the balcony.
Her house near the station was obvious from the bridge.
He has a silver car that his parents bought him.
Tom has a box of chocolate, so he hides it in the cupboard.
Rooms with a northern window often need extra light in winter.

notes: Card: 'need to belong to social groups.', 'appetite for the marvellous was', 'Type B personality', 'sweet tooth,', 'Curiosity', 'love of systems and organization that'. Probe: trait sentences 0.33-1.22 (appetite for adventure 'was' 1.22, sweet tooth 'so' 0.84, love of order 'that' 0.75, curiosity 0.75); same shape with a possession ('a huge garden, so') 0.17; unrelated 0.003-0.008.
